title: 2026 Season Power Rankings
subtitle: Pre-Week 9 board. The Eddies made it six straight and took first on the PF tiebreak, the SPD's dropped 317.5 for the kitty and then traded away a 40-point linebacker days later, Joe Burrow's 58 gave the Dongers a winning streak, and Substation's 70-point defense got them tossed off the bus, leaving six riders. Ultron and Saltese swapped Bijan Robinson for Ashton Jeanty in an eight-player blockbuster, TTAB sent Josh Allen to Ultron, and the Goats grabbed the Last Ride wheel. A light PIT/TEN bye week still parks Patrick Queen, T.J. Watt, Tony Pollard, Jaylen Warren, Amani Hooker and Chimere Dike.
method: W/L + win quality + roster ceiling + FAAB + pedigree + sit/start + trades; PF is evidence, not the ranking.

rankings.blurb: Juice: six straight wins after an 0-2 start, and this time the offense showed up too. The Eddies went into Ultron and won 269–227 behind Brock Bowers (34), Chimere Dike (34 on a 7.5 projection) and Trevor Lawrence (24) for a 126-point offense, plus a 143-point defense led by George Karlaftis (30), Quentin Lake (28), Jordyn Brooks (24), Evan Williams (23) and $4 waiver pickup Cole Bishop (17). That's 6-2, tied with the Goats and first on the PF tiebreak at 2018.0, one of six teams still on the bus, and Breece Hall (quad) is reported good to go against Kansas City. Junk: George Pickens debuted with 6 and Corey Kiner managed 4 filling in for Hall, Dike and Cedric Gray head into the Titans' bye right after Dike's breakout, and Cameron Skattebo, Travis Etienne and Jordyn Tyson are still parked in IR slots. Wednesday's waivers brought in Josh Downs ($7) and Devin Singletary ($2), with Kiner cut to make room ($25 left). TTAB visits with Caleb Williams under center now that Josh Allen lives in Ultron.

Juice: still the WU's scoring machine at 2210.0 PF, 184.5 clear of anyone else, and the 268 they put up Sunday would have beaten nine teams. Amani Hooker (42), Dane Belton (36), Ernest Jones (27) and Trey McBride (25.5) carried a 163-point defense, and the $85 wallet is still the fattest in the league. Junk: that 268 ran straight into the SPD's 317.5, so Pocket has lost two straight and slid to 5-3. Jared Goff posted 10 and Chigoziem Okonkwo 3.5, Hooker heads into the Titans' bye, and Saquon Barkley and Rashid Shaheed are still in IR slots. Next up is a trip to Ultron, which now has Josh Allen and Bijan Robinson in the same lineup.

Juice: won 253–245 over LAB and won Last Ride over TTAB on the same scoreboard, so the Goats are 6-2, tied for first, and holding the Last Ride steering wheel. Patrick Mahomes went from 4 to 42, Bucky Irving (29), Josh Jacobs (25) and Chase Brown (17) built a 136 offense, and T.J. Watt (29) and Devin Bush (24) led the defense. Still the stingiest PA in the WU (1716.5) with $60 in the bank after a $4 Wednesday claim on Mike Gesicki to replace Andrews. Junk: the 1887.0 PF ranks eighth, DK Metcalf (3), Keisean Nixon (4) and Mark Andrews (6, since cut) were dead weight, and Metcalf and Watt both hit the Steelers' bye. Week 9 is a road trip to Doubtpfizer and a Last Ride date with freshly dumped Substation.

Juice: still on the bus, still 5-3, and the defense won its half 136–117 behind Roquan Smith (33) and Jacob Parrish (31), while Jaylen Warren (29) and Puka Nacua (25) did the heavy lifting on offense. Sixth in PF at 1977.0 with $56 left. Junk: back-to-back losses to the Dongers and the Goats, the latter by 8. Jayden Daniels managed 16, Jeremiyah Love scored 3 and is reportedly headed to IR with an ankle, Greg Dulcich lasted one week after his $5 pickup, Mike Evans carries an injury tag, and Warren hits the Steelers' bye. Substation visits, fresh off getting tossed from the bus.

Juice: 317.5! The SPD's took the Week 8 high and the kitty, snapped a three-game skid and knocked off Pocket behind a 206-point defense, best in the WU by 43: Ty'Ron Hopper (40), Eric Wilson (40), Jordan Battle (34), Andrew Van Ginkel (30), Jeremiah Trotter (24) and Nathan Landman (22). Tee Higgins (43), Jordan Love (26) and Matthew Golden (20) handled the offense. Then on Tuesday night, Ryan finally fixed the tight end black hole, sending Wilson and Henry To'oTo'o to Substation for Tyler Warren and Kevin Winston. Junk: yes, that's a linebacker traded away days after scoring 40. Zay Flowers posted a 0, Jordan Mason 3 and Jonathan Taylor 6, A.J. Brown carries an injury tag, Winston is on the Titans' bye, and Davante Adams and TreVeyon Henderson are in IR slots. Hyper hosts in a bus-on-bus showdown.

Juice: two straight wins, back to .500, and second in the WU in PF at 2025.5. Dexter Lawrence (30), Jeremy Chinn (29) and Blake Cashman (25) built a 144-point defense that crushed Substation's 70, and Kirk Cousins (33) led the offense in a 257–203.5 win that kept Hyper on the bus. Junk: the wallet is down to $12, the Micah Parsons stash was cut three days after the $4 bid, Emeka Egbuka and Nick Bosa sit in IR slots, Jacory Croskey-Merritt carries an injury tag, and Payton Wilson hits the Steelers' bye. The 317.5-point SPD's come to town.

Juice: 305, the second-best score of Week 8, and the defense that cratered to 85 last week came roaring back with 148 (Anthony Hill 30, Jeffery Simmons 30, Gregory Rousseau 25, Devon Witherspoon 20). Harold Fannin (36), Jahmyr Gibbs (33), Drake Maye (26) and James Cook (21) built a 157 offense, and the Slumlords are back to 4-4 after handing Doubtpfizer a 69.5-point beating. Junk: still $0 in FAAB, the 2022.0 PA is third-worst in the league, Quinshon Judkins managed 7, and Hill and Wan'Dale Robinson hit the Titans' bye while Isiah Pacheco sits in an IR slot. A trip to Saltese is next.

Juice: fourth in the WU in PF at 2010.0, still on the bus, and still sitting on $72, the second-biggest wallet in the league, after spending $3 on Malik Mustapha in Wednesday's waivers. Alex Singleton followed his 53 with 39, and Braelon Allen (31) and Chuba Hubbard (27) kept the offense respectable. Junk: lost 305–235.5 to the Slumlords, the defense fell from 178 to 111, Kyle Pitts and Byron Young scored 3 apiece, and the 2216.0 PA is the worst in the WU by 118.5. Christian McCaffrey is questionable with a hamstring, Hunter Henry and Reed Blankenship are in IR slots, and Breece Hall's return could eat into Allen's work. The 6-2 Goats visit.

Juice: beat Morningside 213.5–172.5 behind Patrick Queen (42), Harold Perkins (26), Christian Watson (22) and Jameson Williams (19). Chase also pulled off one of the week's big swaps, sending Josh Allen to Ultron for Caleb Williams, Micah McFadden and Queen, who promptly scored 42 in his debut. Junk: the 213.5 lost Last Ride to the Goats' 253, so TTAB's re-entry dream is over. Omar Cooper Jr. posted a 0, Watson carries an injury tag, DeVonta Smith, Brian Branch and Divine Deablo are in IR slots, and Queen heads into the Steelers' bye one week after arriving. A trip to the 6-2 Eddies is next.

Juice: won the offensive half 133.5–113 behind Emmett Johnson (41), Ja'Marr Chase (39) and Tucker Kraft (22), and Nate kept dealing, landing Eric Wilson (fresh off a 40) and Henry To'oTo'o from the SPD's on Tuesday night for Kevin Winston and Tyler Warren. A Last Ride date with the Goats is the only road back onto the bus. Junk: the defense scored 70 (Jack Campbell 3, Tykee Smith 3, DeShon Elliott 2), Tre Tucker posted a 0, and the 203.5 was the low among the alive, so Substation is off the bus. Last week's haul from the Eddies went Bryce Young 13 and Tyler Warren 7.5, and Warren is already gone. Campbell now sits in an IR slot, only $5 is left in the wallet, and a trip to LAB awaits.

Juice: the busiest front office in the WU this week. On Oct 29, Brian landed Bijan Robinson, Omarion Hampton, Kyle Hamilton, Brian Robinson Jr. and $5 from Saltese for Ashton Jeanty, Carson Schwesinger, Kyle Monangai and D'Andre Swift, then sent Micah McFadden, Caleb Williams and Patrick Queen to TTAB for Josh Allen. Allen (30), Michael Wilson (32), Foye Oluokun (31) and Josh Metellus (28) all delivered. Junk: the new-look offense scored 97 in a 269–227 loss to the Eddies (Bijan 9, Hampton 5, Drake London 5, Tyler Higbee 3), Queen dropped 42 for TTAB in the same week, Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Robinson Jr. are in IR slots, and Michael Wilson carries an injury tag. Pocket comes to town.

Juice: Bhayshul Tuten (37), newly acquired D'Andre Swift (30) and Jamien Sherwood (25) did their part, and the defense won its half 119–93. Luke rebuilt the backfield with Jeanty, Swift, Monangai and Carson Schwesinger in the Bijan blockbuster with Ultron, then added Demetrius Knight from Morningside for Terrel Bernard and Denzel Boston. Junk: ran into Joe Burrow's 58 and lost 268–232.5 to the Dongers, falling to 3-5. Matthew Stafford scored 9 and is questionable with an arm injury, Jeanty managed 9, David Walker posted a 0, Tuten carries an injury tag, Jonathon Brooks, RJ Harvey and David Montgomery are in IR slots, and Rico Dowdle hits the Steelers' bye. Wednesday's waivers added Malik Willis ($1) as Stafford insurance and Adonai Mitchell ($1). The Slumlords visit with only $3 left in the Saltese wallet.

Juice: THE DONGERS HAVE A WINNING STREAK. Joe Burrow's 58 was the top player score of Week 8, Tony Pollard (43), JSN (29) and T.J. Hockenson (18.5) powered a 175-point offense (best in the WU by 18), and the 268–232.5 win over Saltese makes it two straight. Their 1837.0 PF now tops four teams with better records. Junk: still 2-6 with $1 to spend, the defense managed 93, Pollard heads into the Titans' bye right after his 43 (Jalen Ramsey too), D.J. Moore carries an injury tag, and Jevon Holland, David Bailey and KaVontae Turpin are in IR slots. Next is a trip to Morningside, which cut both of its quarterbacks this week.

Juice: Lukas Van Ness went from 1 to 27, Malaki Starks added 25 and Jessie Bates 17, and Tim flipped Demetrius Knight to Saltese for Terrel Bernard and Denzel Boston. Junk: four straight losses, the Week 8 floor at 172.5, and a 62.5-point offense with Lamar Jackson's 0, Xavier Worthy's 4 and Ollie Gordon's 8. Lamar is headed for thumb surgery and IR, so Morningside cut him and Jacoby Brissett, and Wednesday's waivers came and went without a quarterback add: as of the 10:15 AM PT sync, there's no QB on the roster. Dead last in PF at 1624.5, 129 behind 13th, with Deebo Samuel and Derwin James in IR slots and $8 left. The Dongers visit with a winning streak, which is a sentence nobody expected to type in Week 9.
